title: IXDE in one kind, both kinds: predators made of a conserved, self-miscible material that condenses only up its own product of digesting prey, on c46's fuel-driven prey; from noise both kinds persist, divide at labkit's default window (predators gen 4 and 3, prey gen 5 and 4), the predators turn a frozen prey emulsion into a dividing, moving one, and each kind dissolves when its own supply is cut while its matter is kept
summary: world.py keeps the prey of 20261026T2103-c46-hunting-ecology-claim (a conserved prey material that condenses only up its own catalysis product, which needs a consumed, regrowing fuel) and replaces its predator: the predator material is conserved (never made from prey, never decays), miscible on its own (r0b 0.3), and condenses only up a product q that it makes by digesting prey material (dig = k2 c_a^2 c_b^2 turns prey material into waste that is remade into prey material; dq = kd dig - q + lap q). c46's nonreciprocal fuel-depletion taxis is kept (chiF 0.5); Mb 0.005. Labkit, 256^2, seeds 0 and 1, t=12000, default lineage window K=20 frames (2000 t): predators sit as comet-shaped bodies on one side of each prey (median 14% of a predator's area inside prey), 81 and 74 persistent predator tracks, 49 and 43 persistent predator splits, generation 4 and 3, merge/split 0.20 and 0.31; prey 65 and 69 persistent splits, generation 5 and 4. Divisions are joint: a prey stretches and pinches while the predator on its waist is drawn out between the two daughters and pinches with it (pred_ancestry.png). The matched predator-free twins are frozen emulsions (155 and 146 prey, 0 persistent splits, 0 and 2 moving tracks). Removing all prey at t=6000 dissolves every predator within ~700 t (54 -> 0-1, 46 -> 0, max c_b 1.48 -> 0.5 -> bath) with the predator material kept; cutting the fuel dissolves every prey within 200 t with the prey material kept, and the predators then fade over 2000 t as they digest the dissolved prey.

claims.statement: In pack256/seed0 and pack256/seed1 (python -m labkit.run world.py --seeds <s> --size 256 256 --frames 120 --no-movie, defaults, K=20), prey condensates form from noise and predator condensates form on them from predator-material noise added at t=2000. The predators, whose material is never made from prey and is miscible without digestion, persist as separate bodies (81 and 74 persistent tracks; overlap lines from t=3000: median survival 2600-2700 t, 19 and 15 of 154 and 148 to t=12000) and divide (49 and 43 persistent splits, generation 4 and 3); the prey persist (97 and 99 persistent tracks) and divide (65 and 69, generation 5 and 4). The predators change prey dynamics against the matched predator-free twin, and each kind dissolves when its own supply is cut (predators when the prey are removed, prey when the fuel is cut) although neither is built from that supply.
claims.track: seed 0, predator track 62 -> 230 -> 365 -> 424 -> 478 (pack256/seed0/pred_ancestry.png, .json): nucleates on a prey at t=2200, persists through four persistent splits at t=3700, 7100, 8600 and 9800 (generation 4) and is alive at t=12000; it exists only while digesting (dfork: every predator dissolves within ~700 t of prey removal) and is one of the predators whose presence turns the twin's frozen prey emulsion into a dividing one

controls_run.X: twin256/seed0 and twin256/seed1 (pred_on 0; same seeds, grid, duration and default window): prey 155 and 146 bodies, 0 persistent splits, generation 0, 2 and 0 moving tracks; with predators prey 195 and 193, 65 and 69 persistent splits, generation 5 and 4, 321 and 324 moving tracks. Sign: predators raise prey body number, division and motion (they cut and stir prey while eating them); prey are required by predators (dfork)
controls_run.E: fork/dfork_s0, dfork_s1 (128^2, dfork_t 6000: all prey material removed, waste no longer remade into prey) vs fork/fed_s0, fed_s1 run alongside (drive.py): predators 54 -> 1 by t=6800 and 46 -> 0 by t=6700, max c_b 1.48 -> 0.51 and 1.45 -> 0.38 by t=7000, mean predator material constant (0.10); fed: 51 and 48 predators. Prey E: fork/ffork_s0, ffork_s1 (fork_t 6000, fuel set to 0 and not regrown): prey 52 -> 0 and 45 -> 0 by t=6200, mean prey material 0.285 -> 0.299 (kept), predators then 54 -> 7 and 46 -> 4 by t=8000 (forks.png)

limits: Divisions of both kinds are joint fissions of a prey-predator pair: the prey pinches and the predator on its waist is drawn out between the daughters and pinches with it (pred_ancestry.png, strict_pred_a10.png); I did not find predators dividing away from prey (splits3.py: 45 and 48 strict predator divisions at min area 10, 20 and 20 at area 20, all with prey within 6 px). Predators are comet-shaped bodies attached to prey (median 14% of area inside prey, 3-4% mostly inside), so a reviewer may weigh whether the pair is the individual. The populations reach a steady coexistence (~190 of each at 256^2), not cycles; the effect of predators on prey body number is positive. The fuel-depletion taxis of the predators is a written nonreciprocal drift (c46's); without it (Mb 0.05 or 0.01, chiF 0) predators nucleate inside prey, eat them and dissolve, with no persistent predator tracks (screens: lks not included; numbers in the sighting). Predator material is added as noise at t=2000 (from t=0 it has no prey to digest). Forks at 128^2 with drive.py counts, not labkit. dt/2 (dthalf/seed0, 128^2, WORLD_P dt 0.1, labkit times read 2x the sim time) gives the same comet pairs and 47 prey / 45 predators at the end against 49 / 47 at dt 0.2 (screens/m3_sheet.png); no grid variant. pack128b/seed2 (128^2, t=12000): 11 persistent predator splits, generation 2; 17 prey, generation 3. Fast predators (k2 0.2, or too much predator material) eat every prey and the prey do not renucleate (screens/fast_predators_extinct.png). No Laplacian-only twin. Predator c_b overshoots to ~1.5 inside bodies (the q term shifts the condensed state).
